transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to get our pre-lock round-robin underway so we can move toward final production approval. Let's go through the standard sequence: technical, rights, talent, and accessibility leads — please report your final operating requirements. I'll need to hear from each of you before I can sign off on the production package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical finding before we proceed. My completed radio-frequency survey found that wireless roaming camera links interfere with the theater's assistive-listening loop. Because of this, the gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms — no wireless roaming cameras. I filed the survey in the technical folder, but I want to make sure everyone is aware it is not currently reflected on Mara's draft lock sheet. This directly affects the current draft package, which lists three cameras, and it also has accessibility implications given the assistive-listening loop.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue before we proceed. I received the countersigned performance license this morning, and it permits the gala broadcast but explicitly prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips. The recording must be marked broadcast-only. This directly conflicts with the current draft package, which permits the recording to be reused in the festival archive. I have not yet entered this restriction in the rights tracker, but it is binding. The festival archive reuse provision in the draft package must be removed before I can approve.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag two critical talent issues before we proceed. First, I confirmed with the headliner's agent that the performer can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM on Saturday — this is not currently reflected in the production schedule. Second, the headliner's rider explicitly prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. I have the agent's confirmation in email. This directly conflicts with the current draft package, which includes a sponsor product display on stage. The sponsor product display on stage must be removed before I can approve.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical accessibility issue before we proceed. My accessibility vendor confirmed that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B, whose dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder. The general control-room location listed in the current draft plan will not work. I documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file, but I have not yet added the booth assignment to the lock sheet. The lock sheet must be updated to assign Booth B for the captioner before I can approve.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.headliner_soundcheck_time: 3:00 PM on Saturday, per Jonah's confirmation with the headliner's agent.
decisions.stage_sponsor_treatment: No sponsor product display on the performance stage — removed from the plan, per the headliner's rider prohibition reported by Jonah.
decisions.captioner_location: Booth B, using its dedicated return feed connected to the gala's caption encoder, per Nia's accessibility vendor confirmation.
